title: Sales enablement playbook: positioning, competitive briefs, pitch decks, pricing guidance, case studies, security FAQ
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s core positioning and messaging, competitive brief summaries, pitch deck guidance, pricing guidance and negotiation levers, customer case studies with measurable outcomes, and a security FAQ tailored for prospective customers. It's intended for AEs, solutions engineers, and GTM partners to run concise, technically credible conversations from discovery through procurement.

Use guidance:
- Refer to the elevator pitches for 30s/2m/5m skus depending on prospect technical sophistication.
- Pull the one-page competitive brief into deal rooms and attach the security FAQ for regulated buyers.
- Use the pricing guidance and discount table when qualifying ARR and procurement timelines.

Key messages (TL;DR):
- Redwood makes LLM inference predictable, cost-efficient, and reliable across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- We optimize production economics (latency + cost) without forcing customers to operate their own fleet or sacrifice control.
- For enterprises, Redwood provides deployment flexibility (VPC/on-prem), auditability (logs, KMS), and SLA-backed performance.

Positioning & messaging (audience-specific):

1) Developer / Startup (technical buyer)
- Primary value props:
  - Fast onboarding: Hosted API and SDKs enable a POC in under 1 day.
  - Performance transparency: model profiles and observable latency-by-route.
  - Cost controls: token-level breakdowns, auto-batching suggestions, and caching features.
- Elevator pitch (30s): "Ship LLM features faster with predictable latency and measurable token economics — Redwood handles batching, caching, and routing so you can iterate on product instead of infra."

2) Platform / Infra Team
- Primary value props:
  - Unified runtime across environments (hosted, dedicated, VPC/private).
  - Operational tooling: tracing hooks, model rollouts, and per-route SLO dashboards.
  - Deterministic performance: quantization profiles and kernel selection tuned per-architecture.
- Elevator pitch (2m): focus on SLAs, autoscaling policies, and predictable capacity.

3) Enterprise / Security Decision Maker
- Primary value props:
  - Private deployments with customer-managed control plane and KMS/HSM integrations.
  - Compliance-ready: audit logs, retention controls, and SOC/ISO artifacts available.
  - Contract flexibility: dedicated capacity, advanced observability, and premium SLAs.
- Elevator pitch (2m): emphasize data residency, encryption in transit and at rest, and auditability.

Differentiators (battle-tested):
- Production-first observability: token and route level cost + latency breakdown — helps customers optimize unit economics.
- Smart routing & graceful degradation: policy-driven routing and fallbacks to model variants reduce outage risk.
- Cost-aware controls: recommendations for batching, caching and quantization with measurable cost impact.
- Unified interface: same API and rollout semantics across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.

Competitive brief (one-page summary):

| Competitor | Typical customer | Strengths | Weaknesses vs Redwood | Positioning guidance |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Cloud AI Endpoints (major clouds) | Enterprises with cloud-native stack | Deep cloud integration, managed GPUs | Higher per-token cost for LLM-scale inference; limited rollout/smart-routing features | Emphasize Redwood’s specialized inference kernel optimizations, unified runtime and developer experience. |
| LLM API Providers (OpenAI, Anthropic) | Product teams wanting fastest TTV | Broad model catalog, strong model R&D | Less flexible deployment (private/air-gapped), limited dedicated capacity options | Lead with deployment flexibility and enterprise controls; quantify cost and latency differentials on representative prompts. |
| Self-hosted inference vendors (open-source runtimes, startups) | Platform teams wanting full control | Low-ish licensing cost, self-management | Operational overhead and lack of hosted fallbacks; lower observability | Sell Redwood as hybrid option: dedicated pools + managed control plane reduces ops burden. |
| Inference infra vendors (specialized) | Large infra orgs | High performance on niche models | Often single-focus; weaker product/SDK surface | Emphasize Redwood Console, eval tooling, and ML-friendly developer docs. |

Competitive battle card (quick rebuttals):
- Prospect: "We can self-host for cheaper."
  - Rebuttal: Self-hosting hides recurring ops cost and risk. Redwood reduces ops with dedicated pools, autoscaling and fallback paths; we can model TCO vs self-host with a 3-year forecast.
- Prospect: "OpenAI/Anthropic have the best models."
  - Rebuttal: Model quality is important — Redwood supports curated open models, verified performance profiles, and fast model rollouts with A/B testing to validate quality in your workload.

Pitch deck guidance (recommended slide flow + speaker notes):
1) Cover / TL;DR (1 slide)
- One-line value statement + 3 bullets: predictable performance, lower unit cost, enterprise controls.

2) Problem (1 slide)
- Common problems: unpredictable latency, unbounded costs, operational complexity, and model regressions in production.

3) Product overview (2 slides)
- Product map: Redwood API, Dedicated, Private, Console, Optimize.
- Short descriptions & when to use each.

4) Architecture (1 slide)
- High-level diagram (describe in speech): client -> smart-routing -> runtime (batching, KV cache) -> hardware. Call out fallbacks and observability hooks.

5) Performance & cost (1 slide)
- Use client-specific benchmark: e.g., median generation latency, tokens/sec, and per-token cost delta vs baseline. Include a 1–2 line case study metric.

6) Security & Compliance (1 slide)
- Bullet KMS/HSM, VPC/private install, audit logs, SOC/ISO artifacts, data residency.

7) Pricing & commercial terms (1 slide)
- High-level bands (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) and procurement guidance.

8) Customer success & onboarding (1 slide)
- Typical timeline: POC (1–2 weeks), pilot at scale (4–8 weeks), production onboarding (1–3 months depending on Dedicated/Private).

9) Next steps & CTA (1 slide)
- Suggest POC triggers, required data for forecasting, and technical contact.

Pricing guidance (playbook for commercial and AE teams):

Pricing structure (high-level):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): per-token generation (prompt + completion) and per-embedding unit.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly or annual commitment for GPU pools (committed throughput) + per-token adjustment for overage.
- Private (enterprise license): platform fee + optional support and maintenance + deployment services.

Example bands (for qualification only; commercial final pricing varies by region and negotiation):
- Hosted SMB: $0.0008 per generated token / $0.0004 per embedding unit.
- Hosted Mid-market: $0.0006 per generated token with volume tiers at 1M, 10M tokens.
- Dedicated: starting at $20k/month committed (multi-GPU pool); discounts for 12/24/36 month terms.
- Private: one-time platform fee (T&M for on-prem) + annual support (typically 15% of platform fee)

Discount levers and negotiation guidance:
- Commit term: 12/24/36 month commits unlock tiered discounts.
- Usage floors: committed throughput vs burst capacity tradeoffs.
- Concierge onboarding and retention: professional services for private deployments.
- Observability add-ons: longer retention windows for logs/metrics as add-on.

Contractual notes for legal handoff:
- Standard SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime for Dedicated pools; escalations documented in SLA addendum.
- Data residency and retention: include options and retention windows in SOW.

Case studies (2 short wins to use in pitch):

1) Acme Retail (B2C ecommerce, Hosted -> Dedicated pilot)
- Problem: slow peak-time inference and unbounded prompt costs during promotions.
- Solution: Deployed Dedicated capacity for pricing API endpoints and enabled prefix caching across sessions.
- Outcome: 45% reduction in per-token cost for promotion traffic, median latency improved from 340ms to 120ms, and cost predictability enabled a 3x scale during events.

2) FinServ Co (regulated enterprise, Private deployment)
- Problem: data residency and E2E audit requirements prevented use of public LLM APIs.
- Solution: Private deployment in VPC with KMS integration, log forwarding to SIEM, and role-based access controls.
- Outcome: Passed internal audit for model-powered features; procurement approved a 24-month Dedicated contract, and time-to-production reduced by 6 weeks vs building in-house.

Security FAQ for prospects (concise Q&A to attach to RFPs):

Q: Where are customer inputs and outputs stored?
A: For Hosted customers, transient request logs and traces are stored in our control plane with retention configurable per-customer; data at rest is encrypted with customer-specific keys where requested. Dedicated pools can be configured to forward logs to the customer’s log ingestion endpoint.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (CMK/KMS)?
A: Yes. Private and Dedicated customers can use KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) or HSM-backed keys for encryption.

Q: Can Redwood run in an air-gapped environment?
A: Yes. Our Private on-prem package supports air-gapped deployments with offline packaging and documented build/artifact checks. Professional services required for initial installation.

Q: How do you handle model provenance and third-party models?
A: We maintain a model catalog with provenance metadata and versioned model artifacts. Customers can pin model versions and opt into Redwood-verified performance profiles.

Q: Is there logging for auditing and compliance?
A: Yes. Audit logs include API request metadata, deployment rollouts, and admin actions. Log retention and export to customer SIEM can be configured.

Q: What certifications/evidence do you provide?
A: We maintain SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts for the control plane; specific evidence packages available under NDA for Dedicated/Private customers.

Q: How do you ensure model output safety and quality?
A: Redwood offers quality guardrails and regression detection tied to prompt sets and evals. We support model rollouts with canary and A/B testing and automated fallback policies.

Objections & responses (sales bullets):
- "We don’t want vendor lock-in."
  - Response: Redwood supports open models and provides exportable model artifacts where possible; our APIs are documented and customers can pin model versions to reduce coupling.
- "We already have a cloud vendor."
  - Response: Redwood complements cloud providers by offering a unified inference runtime optimized for LLM workloads and advanced orchestration features that many cloud endpoints don't provide out-of-the-box.

Meeting playbook (AE + SE choreography):
1) Pre-meeting prep (AE)
- Collect expected qps, typical sequence lengths, and representative prompts.
- Identify compliance requirements and procurement timeline.

2) Discovery (30–45m, joint)
- Validate user journey, SLOs, peak patterns, and cost sensitivity.
- Ask for sample prompts and success metrics.

3) Technical session (SE)
- Show trunked demo (Hosted API), run a quick latency/cost forecast using provided prompts, and present architecture options for Dedicated/Private.

4) Commercial & next steps (AE)
- Share pricing bands, propose POC scope (1–2 weeks hosted or small Dedicated pilot), and assign technical contacts.
